Capture-strategy ablation · gap-aware Chamfer (Accuracy / Completeness / F1)

Does how you film the object change the reconstruction? — 2 objects × 3 capture approaches × 2 methods

Each reconstruction is aligned to its LiDAR reference, density-matched to the reference's median point spacing, and scored with gap-aware Accuracy/Completeness/F1. Drag any cloud to rotate, scroll to zoom. Each object has its own live DBSCAN gap-exclusion tuner; moving a slider recomputes that object's six panels and the summary table & F1 chart below. The three approaches: T1 = close-ups (top+front) plus a wider full-object orbit; T2 = overhead only (straight-on + overhead orbit); T3 = full-object orbit only (object always fully in frame, no close-ups).
Colouring within t (correct)  beyond t heatmap: 0…15 cm LiDAR / reconstruction overlay T1 T2 T3

Summary — object × approach × method

F1 / Accuracy@3cm / Completeness@3cm and the excluded-point count update live with each object's DBSCAN tuner. Accuracy & completeness medians and inlier RMSE@3cm are distributional stats on the density-matched cloud. The best F1 within each (object, method) group is highlighted.

F1@3cm by capture approach

Grouped by (object, method) so the ranking of the three approaches is visible within each configuration — if the same approach colour is tallest in every group, that approach is a method- and object-independent winner.

Is the difference between capture approaches real?

For each object & method: the three pairwise F1 differences (T1−T2, T1−T3, T2−T3) as bootstrap distributions. A distribution lying entirely on one side of 0 means that pair of approaches really differs; one straddling 0 means the difference is within noise.

Interpretation

Capture-approach comparison · outputs/registrations/ (exp_081–092) · references: *_no_floor_centered.ply · density-matched to reference median NN-spacing · gap-aware Chamfer · raw WebGL, no external libraries. Built by src/registration/build_capture_comparison_page.py.
